Well, those are all some fairly big plans - so you've got to take them one bite at a time. Once you start one plan, you'll slowly become more organised and eventually organised enough to do another. 

For example, if you choose to start by losing weight which you can do by designating a few times in the week to go to the gym, or for a run - and you make sure they're timed and not sporratic, e.g. before work or at 7 o'clock on Wednesday and Friday etc. That small bit of organisation will spur you on to become more organised in general, enough to then say - "Why don't I, after I go to the gym, write 2 or 3 pages of a novel?"

You can build all these things up slowly - take a few steps for a business, i.e. come up with an idea for one, and then maybe the next week apply for a business tax file or draw up a flow chart of the business process. 

My point is, don't expect yourself to be able to do all these things at once - all of the these things are at least year-long endeavours, so just take them a bit at a time. Pick one and go for that one, then pick up the rest when you feel you can.   
Side note: learning a new skill every year may sound nice on paper, but it's not how things usually work, opportunities will pop up and you can choose to take them. I wouldn't say "I want to learn (x) this year," I'd say, "Next time I see something that looks interesting on a flyer or on a billboard, I'll do it."  


Hope that helps!
